'''Sarah J. Greenwald''' is professor of mathematics at [[Appalachian State University]] and faculty affiliate of gender, women's and sexuality studies.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://mathsci.appstate.edu/people/sarah-j-greenwald|title=Sarah J. Greenwald|date=2018-02-15|website=Sarah J. Greenwald|language=en|access-date=2020-01-17}}</ref>

==Research==
Greenwald's research interests include [[geometry]] and the [[scholarship of teaching and learning]]. She also investigates connections between mathematics and society, such as women, minorities and popular culture. For example, she was part of a team that looked into allusions to mathematics in ''[[The Simpsons]].''<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://homepage.smc.edu/nestler_andrew/SimpsonsMath.htm|title=Andrew Nestler's Guide to Mathematics and Mathematicians on The Simpsons|website=homepage.smc.edu|access-date=2020-01-17|archive-date=2020-05-03|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200503125404/http://homepage.smc.edu/nestler_andrew/SimpsonsMath.htm|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Education==
In 1991, Greenwald graduated summa cum laude with honors in mathematics from [[Union College]] with a [[Bachelor of Science|BS]] degree.<ref name=cv>{{cite web|title=Sarah J. Greenwald|url=https://mathsci2.appstate.edu/~sjg/resumefull.pdf|publisher=Appalachian State University|access-date=15 February 2021|archive-date=5 July 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160705111018/http://mathsci2.appstate.edu/~sjg/resumefull.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref>
In 1998, she earned a PhD in mathematics at the [[University of Pennsylvania]] in [[Philadelphia, Pennsylvania]]. Her thesis in [[Riemannian geometry]] was entitled ''Diameters of Spherical Alexandrov Spaces and Constant Curvature One Orbifolds'' and was supervised by [[Wolfgang Ziller]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=23168|title=Sarah Greenwald - The Mathematics Genealogy Project|website=genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu|access-date=2020-01-17}}</ref>

==Career==
Greenwald is a professor of mathematics at [[Appalachian State University]] and faculty affiliate of the gender, women's and sexuality studies program there. She has published numerous articles and books in the areas of [[Riemannian geometry]], [[Mathematics education|math education]], and math in society.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.researchgate.net/scientific-contributions/2010349741_Sarah_J_Greenwald|title=Sarah J. Greenwald's research works {{!}} Appalachian State University, NC (ASU) and other places|website=ResearchGate|language=en|access-date=2020-01-17}}</ref> Greenwald has been trying to get young women in [[Girl Scouts of the USA|Girl Scouts]] interested in STEM.  She and Appalachian State colleagues Amber Mellon and Jill Thomley have created a merit badge in mathematics to foster interest in mathematics.<ref>{{cite web |title=ASU Professors Create Girl Scout Badge to Encourage Girls to Pursue Mathematics |url=http://cs.appstate.edu/~sjg/awm/aawmag15.pdf |publisher=Appalachian State University |access-date=23 March 2020 |archive-date=23 March 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200323184616/http://cs.appstate.edu/~sjg/awm/aawmag15.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Greenwald |first1=Sarah J. |last2=Mellon |first2=Amber L. |last3=Thomley |first3=Jill E. |title=Women in Mathematics Badge (Yes, An Actual Badge!) for Girl Scouts |journal=Association for Women in Mathematics Newsletter |date=Jan–Feb 2015 |volume=45 |issue=1 |pages=17–19 |url=https://www.drivehq.com/folder/p8755087/14442180192.aspx |access-date=23 March 2020}}</ref> Greenwald has also created a series of short video interviews of women in STEM who were former Girl Scout members.  This is a work in progress.  Greenwald was elected in 2020 to serve as Member at Large of the Council of the [[American Mathematical Society]] during 2021–2024.<ref>{{cite web |title=American Mathematical Society election results |url=https://www.ams.org/about-us/governance/elections/election-results |access-date=9 December 2020}}</ref>

==Honors==
Greenwald was a 2005 winner of the [[Henry L. Alder Award]] for Distinguished Teaching by a Beginning College or University Mathematics Faculty Member of the [[Mathematical Association of America]] (MAA).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.maa.org/programs-and-communities/member-communities/maa-awards/teaching-awards/henry-l-alder-award|title=Henry L. Alder Award|publisher=[[Mathematical Association of America]]|access-date=2020-02-11|archive-date=2021-02-14|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210214005624/https://www.maa.org/programs-and-communities/member-communities/maa-awards/teaching-awards/henry-l-alder-award|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2017, Greenwald was selected as a plenary speaker at spring southeast section meeting of the MAA at [[Clemson University]] in March 2018.<ref name=clemson>{{cite web | title=Sarah Greenwald selected as MAA Lecturer | website=Sarah Greenwald selected as MAA Lecturer | date=2017-09-05 | url=https://mathsci.appstate.edu/news/sarah-greenwald-selected-maa-lecturer | ref={{sfnref | Sarah Greenwald selected as MAA Lecturer | 2017}} | access-date=2021-02-09}}</ref>
She received the [[Association for Women in Mathematics|AWM]] Service Award in 2018 for her work on the executive committee and as associate editor of the AWM newsletter.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://awm-math.org/awards/awm-service-award/awm-service-award-2018/|title=AWM Service Award 2018|website=Association for Women in Mathematics (AWM)|language=en-US|access-date=2020-01-17}}</ref>  In 2020 she was named a Fellow of the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]].<ref name="Awm-fellow">{{cite web |title=AWM Fellows |url=https://awm-math.org/awards/awm-fellows/2020-awm-fellows |website=Association for Women in Mathematics |publisher=AWM |access-date=17 January 2020}}</ref> Her citation reads "''For her creative and effective efforts to spark interest in mathematics among young people, especially girls; for her extensive contributions to advancing women in mathematics through writing, lectures and working with the AWM and other professional societies; and for her mentorship of students''".  The Mathematical Association of America selected Greenwald as a [[George Pólya]] Lecturer from 2021 to 2022.<ref name=polya>{{cite web | title=Pólya Lectures | website=Mathematical Association of America | url=https://www.maa.org/programs-and-communities/member-communities/maa-awards/lecture-awards/p%C3%B3lya-lecturers | ref={{sfnref | Mathematical Association of America}} | access-date=2021-02-09 | archive-date=2021-01-21 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210121010210/https://www.maa.org/programs-and-communities/member-communities/maa-awards/lecture-awards/p%C3%B3lya-lecturers | url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Publications==
Greenwald co-edited with [[Jill Thomley]] the 3-volume ''Encyclopedia of Mathematics & Society,''<ref>{{cite book |title=The Encyclopedia of Mathematics and Society (3 volumes) |date=October 2011 |isbn=978-1-58765-844-0 |edition=1st |publisher=Salem Press |location=Pasadena, CA}}</ref> which was named a "Best Reference of 2011" by ''[[Library Journal]] and'' was reviewed extensively.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Bemis|first=Michael|date=February 15, 2012|title=Review of Encyclopedia of Mathematics and Society|journal=Library Journal|volume=137|issue=3|pages=127}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Karaali|first=Gizem|date=September 2013|title=Review of Encyclopedia of Mathematics and Society|journal=The College Mathematics Journal|volume=44|issue=4|pages=332–335|doi=10.4169/college.math.j.44.4.332|s2cid=218548986}}</ref> She also co-edited the 2018 Springer volume ''Women in Mathematics: Celebrating the Centennial of the [[Mathematical Association of America]].''<ref>{{cite book |title=Women in Mathematics: Celebrating the Centennial of the Mathematical Association of America |date=4 September 2018 |publisher=Springer-Verlag |isbn=978-3319883038 |edition=1st }}</ref>  She was part of the cast in 'Futurama': Bite My Shiny Metal X<ref>{{Citation|title='Futurama': Bite My Shiny Metal X|url=http://www.imdb.com/title/tt1230103/|access-date=2020-01-26}}</ref> and served as a consultant on Flatland: The Movie.<ref>{{Citation|title=Flatland: The Movie|url=http://www.imdb.com/title/tt0814106/|access-date=2020-01-26}}</ref>
